classification.difficultyReason: Represent reciprocal roots, obtain the third root from their product, and combine the pair-product and sum equations before solving a quadratic.

content.prompt:
Two of the roots of $4x^3+ax^2-47x+12=0$ are reciprocals.

Find the value of $a$ and the three roots.

answer.worked:
Let the roots be $\alpha$, $\frac1\alpha$ and $\beta$.

Product of roots:
$$\begin{aligned}\alpha\cdot\frac1\alpha\cdot\beta&=-\frac{12}{4}\\\beta&=-3\end{aligned}$$
Sum of roots:
$$\begin{aligned}\alpha+\frac1\alpha+\beta&=-\frac a4\\\alpha+\frac1\alpha-3&=-\frac a4\\\alpha+\frac1\alpha&=3-\frac a4\qquad(1)\end{aligned}$$
Sum of products taken two at a time:
$$\begin{aligned}1-\frac3\alpha-3\alpha&=-\frac{47}{4}\\1-3\left(\alpha+\frac1\alpha\right)&=-\frac{47}{4}\\\alpha+\frac1\alpha&=\frac{17}{4}\qquad(2)\end{aligned}$$
From (2):
$$\begin{aligned}4\alpha^2-17\alpha+4&=0\\(4\alpha-1)(\alpha-4)&=0\\\alpha&=\frac14\text{ or }4\end{aligned}$$
Substitute (2) into (1):
$$\begin{aligned}\frac{17}{4}&=3-\frac a4\\a&=-5\end{aligned}$$
Thus $a=-5$ and the roots are $4$, $\frac14$ and $-3$.
